```{r}
getwd()
con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "data/scout.db")
postings = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "scout_postings") |> tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

jobs = postings |>
  dplyr::select(company, title, location_state, remote, category, posted_at, last_seen_at) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::ends_with("_at"), as.Date),
                days_open = as.numeric(last_seen_at - posted_at))

# For Q1, to answer it, you need the following:
# - number of jobs
# - fraction of those jobs that are remote friendly


jobs |> 
  dplyr::group_by(category) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    postings = dplyr::n(), #counting the number of rows per category
    remote_share = mean(remote) |> round(3)
  )

#  Q2 Among the fulltime jobs, which states have the highest remote share?
jobs |> 
  dplyr::filter(category== 'fulltime') |> 
  dplyr::group_by(location_state) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    postings = dplyr::n(), #counting the number of rows per category
    remote_share = mean(remote) |> round(3)
) |> 
  dplyr::filter(postings >= 50) |> #up to you to determine the min threshold
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(remote_share))


jobs |> 
  dplyr::group_by(title) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(
    postings = dplyr::n(), #counting the number of rows per category
    remote_share = mean(remote) |> round(3),
    median_days_open = median(days_open))
  
by_state |> dplyr::left_join(states, by = "location_state")    # keep every row on the left
by_state |> dplyr::inner_join(states, by = "location_state")   # keep only the matches
by_state |> dplyr::anti_join(states, by = "location_state")    # keep only the non-matches

con = DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), "../data/midwest_airbnb.db")
listings = DBI::dbReadTable(con, "listings") |>
  tibble::as_tibble()
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
dplyr::glimpse(listings)

listings |> 
  dplyr::group_by(city)
```
